The Gordie Howe International Bridge, a massive infrastructure project connecting Windsor and Detroit, was set for a joint celebration. Now, Canada will mark the milestone alone to avoid friction with the U.S. administration.

Local dignitaries still get to celebrate the completion of a vital infrastructure project that will improve regional logistics regardless of federal posturing.

The error is in the WHY (Lyrical). The stated reason is diplomatic protest, but the actual reason is political risk management. It is a bait-and-switch of intent.

By framing a logistical necessity as a moral protest, the government avoids the vulnerability of a joint event. This projection of strength masks a deeper inability to navigate bilateral strain.

When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Lesser Evil. The logic ignores the bridge's purpose to serve a political narrative.
